title: First time creating a mobile game, but I need honest advice
author: Daedarion
selftext:
Hi guys, 

I realize that I will probably be roasted in the comments but I need some honest advice.

I've always wanted to make my own game, and I thought as my first game I'll try to make a mobile game. So here I am, 1 month and a half later, I got the system down, I was working on the UI, and a friend of mine actually gave me some valuable feedback, and ever since now it's been gnawing at me.

I've been using AI artwork for everything so far, especially the UI. Today I wanted to upgrade my character and give it much needed attention in terms of looks, animations and whatnot so I contacted a freelancer to get that sorted. The difference between a 128 px character and what AI had created for me is massive, and as a new dev I completely overlooked this.. 

My question is, what are my chances if I get fully animated pixelart main character, and pixelart enemies, but the UI remaining would stay from AI. How likely is my game to get review bombed to oblivion simply because of the use of AI? The UI blends together well but it is quite obviously higher res and ai made.

I cannot attach images here unfortunately, but just honest feedback is appreciated, in case anyone has been in my shoes as well. I rather be sure before I spend hundreds of dollars on more assets, replacing the ai made stuff, including 1000 dollars on just the main character and its animations.

Thank you.

comments.author: tipsystatistic
comments.body: Make the best game you can and enjoy the process. Don’t worry about things you can’t control. AAA games get review bombed.

comments.author: kaizersozeroll
comments.body: Apologies, I don’t have a strong answer for your direct question because I’m slightly behind you in my games development. I think people are mostly upset with deceptive use of ai. There are a lot of people like you and me vibe coding games for the first time. There might be a flood in the market of ai and ai assisted games, at which point they aren’t going to be able to slander every single thing that comes out. It will be eventually expected and all that will matter is if the game is fun to play. You probably shouldn’t hide ai use.

replies.author: Daedarion
replies.body: My worry isn't necessarily the AI use. I worry more about me trying to make the game look pretty, then investing in freelancers to make main character have amazing animations and whatnot, and then in the play store getting a ton of negative reviews because of AI art use. So future players won't even install or try it based on that, even though the game play might be fun.

replies.author: kaizersozeroll
replies.body: Don’t invest more than you are willing to lose. But if you really like and believe in your game I think it’s worth a little investment. Just don’t use your rent and grocery money to clean it up

comments.author: Im_Action
comments.body: nobody would review bomb for Ai unless it was extremely obvious and alot of people still cant tell, the real challenge with mobile games is trying to stand out enough in a genre where 100s of games are published a day in your same category

comments.author: KhaosPT
comments.body:
This is a very subjective thing and will depend on your prompting skills and models you are using. Images and illustrations done by gtp2 are usually very recognizable due to the grainy, yellow tint and that cartoonist round thing it tends to prefer for illustrations. If you prompt it well enough and maybe do a post processing with another model it might not be recognizable. With other models I don't think you would see it. Bur the prompt and your direction dictates more than if you are using AI or not. I can prob post it on test game subs to get some feedback if you are this concerned, before venturing into the app store.

I agree with the other poster, do the best game you can.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
Just make a fun game, a game where you would enjoy playing it. You wouldn't believe I made the STUPIDEST fucking game and people seem to enjoy it, but the game I spent hundreds of hours making no one knows exists.

In both games I used gemini for my sprite sheets. People are gonna shit on you no matter what you do or how amazing your game is either way, just take what people say with a grain of salt.

https://preview.redd.it/iupqrafxo4uh1.jpeg?width=1024&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=7a6aa4e88ce645522d492e6f7e0d1448b7872cd2

comments.author: Jumentous6
comments.body: As a gamer, consistency in what I'm interacting with is important. If the freelance art ends up at a different quality level to the AI created UI, then that would be hard on the eye and could be off putting. As a game developer, I would always aim for a consistent art style, do you know how you want the game to look? Start from there and make that echo through all aspects of the game. Get the UI in front of the artist so they can work to what you have and keep the consistency! I don't think having AI and real art = review bombing

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
err, my first mobile game flopped completely and the submission process was long and tedious. 

the mobile game market is really saturated and you got companies specializing in pumping out mobile games for profit. 

It is a tough crowd
